simcompR: Block-Diagram Simulation of Dynamical Systems in R

simcompR builds and simulates block diagrams in R, in the spirit of Simulink and Python’s bdsim. A model is a graph of blocks connected by signal wires. It is compiled into an execution plan and then simulated:

model, connections, compilation (sizes, feedthrough graph, execution order), continuous integration, sample hits, events, results.

Continuous dynamics are integrated with deSolve. Discrete blocks run at exact sample times, several rates can be mixed, zero crossings are located by root finding, and algebraic loops are detected (and, on request, solved).

Installation 

# install.packages("remotes")
remotes::install_github("adamrsophie/simcompR")

Quick start

A proportional controller with a saturating actuator and a first-order plant:

library(simcompR)

m <- sim_model("loop", params = list(K = 4))
sim_add_block(m, "step", "reference", time = 1)
sim_add_block(m, "subtract", "error")
sim_add_block(m, "gain", "controller", gain = sim_param("K"))
sim_add_block(m, "saturation", "actuator", lower = -2, upper = 2)
sim_add_block(m, "transfer_function", "plant", num = 1, den = c(0.5, 1))
sim_connect(m, "reference", "error", input = 1)
sim_connect(m, "plant", "error", input = 2)
sim_connect(m, "error", "controller")
sim_connect(m, "controller", "actuator")
sim_connect(m, "actuator", "plant")

plan <- sim_compile(m)          # sizes, feedthrough graph, execution order
r <- sim_run(plan, c(0, 5))
plot(r, c("reference", "plant", "actuator"))

# same structure, different gain
r2 <- sim_run(sim_set_params(plan, K = 10), c(0, 5))

The loop through plant is legal because a strictly proper transfer function has no direct feedthrough. A loop made only of gains and sums is an algebraic loop and is reported at compile time.

What is implemented

Area Features
Models blocks, named and numbered ports, connections, model parameters, copies, editing
Compilation size propagation, direct-feedthrough graph, Tarjan components, deterministic order, plan reuse
Continuous integrator, transfer function, state space, general and autonomous ode blocks; deSolve methods that can stop at given times (all but radau, iteration and ode23)
Discrete unit delay, zero-order hold, discrete integrators, discrete state space and transfer functions
Multirate several sample rates and offsets, exact hit times, outputs before updates, rate notes
Hybrid scheduled and zero-crossing events, resets, events on subsystem internals, located kinks of saturation and similar blocks, switch, relay, stop, event limits
Algebraic loops detection with a printed cycle; optional Newton solution with starting values and diagnostics
Structure reusable subsystems, nesting, parameter namespaces, parameter expressions
Logic state machines with guards, priorities, timed transitions, actions
Experiments parameter sweeps, Monte Carlo with fixed seeds, seeded noise, optional parallel runs
Files versioned JSON with exact numbers; non-portable content refused, expressions whitelisted
Results signals, states, events, data frames, plots, diagnostics, DOT export

Not implemented: graphical editing, code generation, physical (acausal) modeling, consistent DAE initialization, buses. See the known limitations and the roadmap in NEWS.md.

Validation

The test suite compares simulations with closed-form answers: exponential decay, harmonic motion, the matrix exponential, second-order step responses, discrete recurrences, sampled control against exact zero-order-hold discretization, multirate timelines and bouncing ball impact times. It runs on Linux, macOS and Windows for every change. vignette("validation") reproduces the comparisons.

Documentation

Fifteen vignettes cover the package from a first model to custom blocks; start with vignette("simcompR") or the website.

Related packages

simcompR belongs to a family of R packages by the same author: symcompR (symbolic computation), modelcompR (equation-based modeling), jaxR (differentiable computation), z3r (constraint solving), optcompR (optimization), graphlearnR, pdecompR (finite elements) and controlcompR (control). simcompR works on its own; integrations are planned and will stay optional.
